session_settled: bmo. Loews' own release of 2026-10-13 gives Monday 2026-11-02 and says the release and earnings remarks go up on loews.com that day (https://s203.q4cdn.com/873173963/files/doc_news/Loews-Corporation-to-Release-Third-Quarter-2026-Results-on-November-2-2026-2026.pdf). It does not state the hour. CNA's co-release says 'before the market opens on Monday, November 2, 2026' (https://finviz.com/news/401924/cna-financial-to-report-third-quarter-2026-results-on-november-2). All 7 of Loews' prior 8-K item 2.02 acceptance times in the baseline are bmo. Q2 2026 came out at 6:00 AM ET (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/CNA). The window is the 2026-10-30 close to the 2026-11-02 close.
conviction_note: The non-result is close to the right answer. Loews has no sourced consensus and its stock moves a median 0.96% on prints. The print turns on CNA's (~90%-owned) underlying combined ratio and cat load. On those, the counterparty evidence is mixed: peers' Q3 cats were higher year on year against CNA's record-low $41m Q3 2025, and commercial pricing is cooling against loss trend. Against that, CNA's sell-side bar ($1.19-1.23 core EPS) is conservative: CNA beat a $1.04 Q2 bar by 14%, and US hotel RevPAR rose 7% in Q3. The findings sum to -0.25, and p_up of 48 on abs_move 1.8 gives -0.07. The two measurements agree in sign and are both near zero.
bar: There is no sourced Loews consensus. One calendar shows no estimate, only the year-ago $2.43 (Q3 2025 EPS, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60086/000006008625000177/exhibit991-q32025.htm), so every Loews-level size is capped small. The operative bar is CNA's Q3 2026 core EPS of about $1.19 (Benzinga / Zacks Research, cut from $1.21 in mid-August, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CNA/earnings-forecasts) to $1.23 (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CNA/estimates). That compares with $1.50 core in Q3 2025. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against CNA core EPS of about $1.21.
positioning_check: Short interest is 4.51M shares, 3.8 days to cover, as of 2026-09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/l). That is about 2% of shares outstanding (204.4M at 2026-06-30) and not crowded. The trend is down from 4.4M / 5.5 days on 2026-08-19 and 7.0 days on 2026-04-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/l/shortinterest). Fintel's 11.3 days looks stale. Options: the chain is unusable (ATM spread 157% of mid, total OI 110) and there is no skew number, so the market makes no directional statement. Tape: +5.47% over 20 days, -0.16% over 5 days, 6.3% below the 52-week high, 20-day realised vol 14.8%.

findings.finding: US commercial peers that reported Q3 2026 took higher catastrophe losses than a year ago: Travelers $538m pre-tax vs $402m, W. R. Berkley $85.9m vs $78.5m, Chubb $705m vs $285m. CNA's Q3 2025 cat was a record-low $41m (all-in combined ratio 92.8%, record core $409m / $1.50). CNA's Q3 2026 cat therefore likely rises year on year, and Loews' consolidated EPS likely prints below last year's $2.43, which is the only visible 'bar' for Loews itself.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (2026-05-04): Loews EPS fell year on year ($1.63 vs $1.74), CNA's combined ratio rose to 102.2% and there was adverse prior-year development; L fell 5.86%. Cats were flat year on year in that quarter ($97m both years), so the drop was on underwriting quality, not cat. Q3 2025: CNA's light-cat record quarter bought only -0.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. CNA's sell-side consensus ($1.19-1.23 vs $1.50 a year ago) already assumes a year-on-year decline. What is not anchored is Loews' own headline: with no Loews consensus, the comparison a reader sees on the wire is the year-ago $2.43. If the market had fully absorbed a lower headline, L would not have run up 5.5% into the print.
findings.independence: Same direction from W. R. Berkley's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000011544/000001154426000046/wrb93020268-kex991.htm) and Chubb Q3 2026 coverage (https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/breaking-news/chubb-shrinks-us-large-account-book-amid-soft-market-594347.aspx). Pointing the other way: Gallagher Re says global 9M26 insured cat losses were the lowest since 2019, with US severe convective storms at ~$43bn (https://www.artemis.bm/news/gallagher-re-estimates-global-insured-cat-losses-at-92bn-for-9m26-lowest-since-2019/). This is a proxy; CNA itself has not spoken on Q3 cats.

findings.finding: CNA's sell-side bar is conservative. Q2 2026 core EPS printed $1.19 against a $1.04 consensus (+14%), even after a $77m after-tax mass-tort charge. Q3 2026 consensus is $1.19-1.23, and Zacks cut it from $1.21 in mid-August. Q2 core excluding the charge was about $1.47/share, and CNA guided Q3 fixed-income investment income to about $575m. The bar therefore leaves room for a higher cat load and still a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-03): CNA beat by 14% and L moved +0.21%. Q3 2025: CNA's record core $1.50 beat ('CNA beats analysts' expectations', theinsurer.com) and L moved -0.14%. On this name, CNA beats have bought almost nothing.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus drifted down after Q2 (Zacks cut to $1.19) despite the Q2 beat. If the street had priced CNA's run-rate, Q3 estimates would sit nearer $1.35-1.45. That is a statement about CNA's bar, not about L's price; L's 5.5% run-up may already hold some of it.
findings.independence: The Q2 earnings remarks give the $575m Q3 fixed-income guide and show the $77m charge was the Q2 annual mass-tort review, already done (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021175/000002117526000043/q22026ex994earningsremarks.htm). This shares a CNA-centred document base with the next finding.

findings.finding: CNA's underlying underwriting trend is deteriorating, and the Q3 peer evidence says loss trend is still outrunning rate. In Q2 2026 CNA's underlying combined ratio was 94.2% vs 91.7%, renewal premium change was slightly above 2% with flat rate, and management raised 2026 underlying loss picks because 'aggregate loss cost trends exceed[ed] rate'. In Q3: Travelers' Business Insurance underlying combined ratio was 88.9% vs 88.3%, its domestic rate ex-National Accounts was +0.9% vs +4.3%, and Chubb said casualty pricing lags loss costs. CNA's Q3 2026 underlying combined ratio will likely sit about 2.5-3 points above Q3 2025's 91.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: underlying deterioration plus adverse development, L -5.86% (largest move in 7 prints). Q2 2026: underlying 94.2% vs 91.7% but core beat, L +0.21%. The line has moved L once, when paired with reserve development.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q2 deterioration is public, and the raised loss picks mean a ~94% underlying is roughly what CNA told the market to expect. That is why this is small. The unpriced part is whether Q3 commercial pricing deceleration (TRV +0.9% rate) pushes it further. A fully priced view would show L lagging P&C peers, not up 5.5% in 20 days.
findings.independence: Travelers Q3 (https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/breaking-news/travelers-q3-2026-record-investment-income-masks-cooling-commercial-pricing-593915.aspx) and Chubb Q3 (https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/breaking-news/chubb-shrinks-us-large-account-book-amid-soft-market-594347.aspx) are separate sources. Counter-evidence: Selective's Q3 10-Q shows lower current-year casualty loss costs and no adverse PYD (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000230557/000023055726000027/sigi-20260930.htm).

findings.finding: Loews Hotels faces an easy comparison and a strong industry quarter. CBRE (2026-10-26) puts Q3 2026 US hotel RevPAR at +7.0% (ADR +4.3%, occupancy 67.7%, +1.8 points). Loews Hotels lost $3m in Q3 2025 and grew Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA 26% to $137m, with management saying 'there is still ramp ahead' at the Universal Orlando properties.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hotels have never been the line L traded on. Q2 2026 hotel net income rose 71% and L moved +0.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: The CBRE series is four days old and Loews has no sell-side hotel model. The size is small because hotels are roughly $50-150m of quarterly EBITDA against a roughly $23bn market cap. Net of the rest of the company (CNA about 60-70% of earnings), the segment cannot carry the print. The resort location type was weakest per CBRE.
findings.independence: Q2 remarks on the Orlando ramp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000060086/000006008626000045/exhibit992-q22026.htm). The CBRE series is an industry proxy, not a Loews number.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 equity markets were narrow: S&P 500 +2.0-2.3% but the equal-weight index -2.2%. That points to a weaker contribution from Loews' parent trading portfolio and from CNA's common-stock and limited-partnership returns than in Q2. Q2 CNA NII of $701m was lifted by LP and common-stock returns, and Q3 2025 Loews corporate income fell to $42m from $73m on weaker trading-portfolio income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Investment-income swings have not been identified as the driver of any of the 7 baseline reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission with an unknown mix in the parent portfolio, and CNA's LP income may be recorded with a lag. The size is small for that reason.
findings.independence: Equal-weight -2.2% and breadth (311 of ~500 down) per https://cryptobriefing.com/sp-500-q3-big-tech-carries-index/. Proxy only.

findings.finding: Q3 has fewer CNA reserve-review triggers than Q1/Q2. The mass-tort review was completed in Q2 ($77m charge) and the A&EP review is scheduled for Q4. Q3 carries only the Life & Group annual assumption update, which cost about $7m after tax in Q3 2025 (secondary source). Peers' Q3 prior-year development was benign: Travelers $234m favourable, and Selective had no net adverse casualty PYD vs $35m adverse a year earlier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 adverse PYD went with L -5.86%. The Q2 corporate charge (mass tort) was absorbed and L moved +0.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: The review calendar is public. This lowers the tail of a reserve shock in this window and does not predict a release. Small, and symmetric-to-positive.
findings.independence: Travelers PYD (https://insurancenewsnet.com/oarticle/travelers-reports-excellent-third-quarter-and-year-to-date-results-3). Selective 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000230557/000023055726000027/sigi-20260930.htm). Shares the CNA Q2 remarks document with finding 2.

findings.finding: Boardwalk's earnings are growing steadily on recontracting rates and completed growth projects: Q2 2026 net income $100m vs $88m, EBITDA $279m vs $274m, Q1 2026 $159m vs $152m, and Q3 2025 was $94m vs $77m. The Spire Marketing acquisition (agreed 2026-03-30) adds marketing volumes, with acquisition costs in Q2. The Q3 2026 contribution is likely up again year on year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Boardwalk grew in every one of the last quarters, including Q1 2026 when L fell 5.86%. It has not been the swing line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a trend continuation the market has seen for several quarters, so it is mostly priced and sized small.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 Loews release figures (https://s203.q4cdn.com/873173963/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/Q1-2026-LC-Earnings-Release-Website.pdf). Same company documents, not independent.

findings.finding: Buybacks continue to shrink the share count. Loews bought 1.4M shares for $146m in Q2 2026 (1.7M / $179m year to date), shares outstanding were 204.4M vs 206.0M at year-end, and the parent held $4.4bn of cash and investments against $1.8bn of debt. That supports per-share book value ($93.52 at 6/30) and the Q3 repurchase figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback disclosures have accompanied every print and none produced a move on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Known policy. Only the Q3 pace is new, and nothing public shows it.
findings.independence: Same Q2 release as findings 3 and 4 (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3608819/loews-corporation-reports-net-income-of-444-million-for-the-second-quarter-of-2026).

outside_window.finding: CNA's A&EP reserve review is scheduled for Q4 2026, a known reserve-shock event that resolves with Q4 results in early 2027.

Hurricane Isaias (outside Gallagher Re's 9M26 window, so in Q4) is expected to generate low-to-mid single-digit billions of insured losses. It lands in CNA's Q4 cats, not this print, though management may comment on it.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew. The +5.5% 20-day run-up into a print where CNA will likely show higher cats and a worse underlying ratio than a record Q3 2025 is a mild tension against longs. CNA's low bar and history of beats cut the other way, and L's damped reaction history (median 0.96%) argues for a small number either way.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): CNA beats bought +0.21% (Q2 2026) and -0.14% (Q3 2025), so the conservative-bar finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.2 and p_up moved from 49 to 48.
Rule 9 (net of the rest): the hotels finding was cut from +0.2 to +0.15 because the segment is small against CNA's share of earnings.
Rule 6 (bar): the Loews bar is unsourced, so all Loews-level sizes stay capped small. The CNA bar has two roughly agreeing sources ($1.19 / $1.23) and was used for print_vs_bar_pct.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked before the negatives (3.8 days, about 2% of shares), not crowded, so no shrink applied.
Rule 5 (proxies): the cat, hotel and equity-market findings were already filed small as proxies; nothing changed.
